articleTitle: About Measurement System in Stations and Substations using Original Data Acquisition Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The paper deals with a method and measurement system designed for the simultaneous monitoring and recording of time variations of electric quantities with no inter-correlation requirements. The method and measurement system were obtained by realizing a multi-unit data acquisition system (MUDAS), relying on at most 3 independent data acquisition systems which operate jointly, in a synchronous way, by means of a synchronizer. Because each of the individual data acquisition system can acquire data for at most 8 electrical quantities (4 voltages and 4 currents), the maximum total number of electrical quantities to be monitored, acquired, and transferred simultaneously to a central control unit is equal to 24. The sampling rate allows for the determination of power quality parameters according to existing standards. MUDAS can also be used in a structure with only 2 individual data acquisition system, in order to simultaneously acquire and display at most 16 electrical quantities. Two examples of utilization of MUDAS are presented.

articleTitle: Computing and Analysing PQ Indices for a Consumer with Various Sources of Harmonics and Non-symmetries
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The paper presents a detailed analysis of certain operating regimes that appear for a consumer with various sources of harmonics and non-symmetries. The analyzed waveforms were acquired with a portable dedicated data acquisition system and transferred to a laptop for processing with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Wavelet Packed Transform (WPT). Small differences (FFT vs WPT) were noticed between the computed values of the power quality indices, due to the non-sinusoidal and sometimes non-symmetric nature of the studied regimes and discrete nature of the processed data respectively. The FFT analysis revealed significant non-symmetrical regimes, as great weights for harmonic orders multiple of 3 were found in the three-phase currents waveforms. Reversed flow of active and reactive powers were noticed. A comparative study of the energies produced by current harmonics was made and discussed. A non-symmetry of the consumer as a whole was detected as well.

articleTitle: Antenna Arrays with Radiating Element a Symmetrical Dipole
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: In the present paper, the analysis of phased antenna arrays made in microstrip technology that can be arranged on an aircraft/UAV is proposed. The antenna arrays will have as a radiating element a symmetrical dipole, the dimensions of the analyzed antenna arrays will be 2x2 and 4x4, with a working band of [4–6] GHz, a gain that increases directly proportional to the number of elements reaching the maximum value of about 12 dB, the input impedance of the antenna arrays of 50Ω and to obtain a good match the VSWR - Voltage Standing Wave Ratio is considered to be less than 2. The design algorithm of the radiating element will be described, the parameters that will be analyzed: the reflective coefficient, the gain and the opening angle of the antenna arrays. Also, 2x2 and 4x4 antenna array structures will be analyzed. It is desired to highlight the advantages of an antenna array, such as the increase in gain directly proportional to the number of elements, the selectivity of the opening angle of the directivity characteristic. These advantages are paramount in the field of aircraft radars because the structure of the antenna arrays is desired to be as simple and light as possible with better performance and selectivity. With the help of this type of symmetric antenna arrays structure, the monopulse tracking system, a system often found in radars on multirole aircraft, can be implemented. The design and analysis of structures made using microstrip technology will be developed within the Ansys Ansoft-HFSS V15.0 design and simulation program.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring of Environment Radiation with Arduino Wemos and Geiger Counter Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: A remote radiation monitoring system is proposed. A method for measuring and analyzing the background radiation level in a given space is developed, based on a Geiger-Müller sensor. The radiation values recorded in a time span can be considered a starting point in establishing the radiation level in a certain location. The occurrence of programmable microcontrollers and different sensors has made possible the creation of low-cost measurement and control systems. Such a data measurement system can be used for monitoring background radiation with an Arduino-based system, and more specifically with a Wemos D1 R1 development board. The radiation monitoring system can collect data from a Geiger-Müller Counter, able to capture the beta particles and gamma rays of the background environment. The data collected by the processor from the Geiger-Müller sensor are transmitted via a wireless connection to a remote ThingSpeak server, where they can be further processed to provide information about the radiation level. Here they can be stored in order to make them available to anyone interested in the evolution of the radiation level over time, for a specific area. As ThingSpeak can provide readings over multiple channels, more radiation sensors can be monitored simultaneously.

articleTitle: On the Distorting Regime at the Connection of Photovoltaic Plants to Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The paper deals with theoretical and practical aspects related to the photovoltaic (PV) systems operation. Their wide utilization in the last years brings a lot of benefits but also exhibits drawbacks related to non-sinusoidal regimes and stability of the systems to which are connected. Particular aspects related to the integration of a photovoltaic system in an islanded network, respectively in an infinite power network, are addressed. The voltages and currents near the inverter, near the PV panels and near the grid to which the PV system is connected are studied. The harmonic decompositions of voltages and currents from various points of the system are analyzed. Voltage and current filtering solutions and the method of connecting active filters are analyzed. The influence of the filters on the various connection points of the active filters is approached, establishing optimal active compensation solutions.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Conducted Emissions Assessment for Electric Powertrain
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The conducted emissions (CE) in powertrain applications are a major concern due to the high current peaks and transients from torque profiles and sudden speed changes. This paper investigates the time-domain noises analytically through a curve-fitting process, whose results can be used to reproduce the noise waveforms avoiding the need to store the entire waveform. Besides, common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) voltages from speed changes of a PMSM (permanent magnet synchronous motor) powertrain are compared, in terms of harmonic components and noise amplitude, by using line impedance stabilization network (LISN) according to different standards. It was observed that DM emissions, at low frequencies, are better coupled to DO-160G LISN and increase progressively with speed rise, while CM noise levels are kept constant.

articleTitle: Conceptual Proposal for an IAK-52 Aircraft Simulation Workstation
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: This paper proposes a concept for developing a flight workstation that can ensure the training capability of military pilots, by simulating flight conditions with IAK-52 type aircraft. The workstation’s specific mission is to provide a training framework for aircrew in operations and maneuvers specific to flying the IAK-52 aircraft through virtual training. The advantages and capabilities proposed by the development of the workstation for the IAK-52 plane are: raising to new training standards for the novice pilots by diversifying the training program; increasing the quality of training in safe conditions and making material and financial savings; the possibility of training to solve special situations that may arise on board the aircraft; ensuring pilot training in different weather conditions; creation of a simulated aerodynamic model corresponding to the IAK-52 aircraft; pilot training in real navigation missions using digital charts; the formation of skills and automatisms through the very precise replication of the cabin, contacts, control elements, levers and levers in the cabin. The current work aims to provide an overview of how to realize the training station by presenting the component elements of the system and by indicating how to connect, place and use them to obtain a functional product, as close as possible to the characteristics of the airplane IAK-52.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Short-Circuited Microstrip Dipole on Different Dielectric Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: This paper aims to analyze and compare the performance of a symmetric dipole antenna made in microstrip technology, on different dielectric substrates to observe the performance of the dielectric substrate in the case of the performance of an antenna that aims to be implemented in a radio link system for UAV/ aircraft. In order to be able to state which frequency band has the designed symmetrical dipole, as well as the effect of the dielectric substrate on its performances, the following parameters of interest will be analyzed: VSWR - Voltage Standing Wave Ratio; impedance value; antenna gain and aperture angle corresponding to the directivity characteristic. This work aims to highlight the influence of the dielectric substrate on the performance of the symmetric dipole antenna made in microstrip technology. And the antenna type analysis aims to design the radiating element of a two-dimensional antenna network that can be implemented in the aeronautical field. The microstrip technology implies by its geometry a structure with low weight and small dimensions that can be embedded on the UAV/aircraft. So dimensions and weight are two very important criteria in the aeronautical field, the lighter the aircraft, the more maneuverable and operational it is.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Electric Field Measurement Experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The paper presents a study on the degree of electromagnetic field exposure of workers in electric power distribution stations. For this purpose, they performed a series of tests on electricity transmission cables used in transformer stations. Based on the results obtained from the experimental testing carried out, the levels of exposure to the influences of the electric and magnetic fields existing in the area where these cables are located were determined. This study is of interest because the maximum limits are regulated by Decision of the Romanian government HG 520/2016 of July 20, 2016 and Directive 2013/35/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013. So, the comparison of the maximum limits allowed in the standard with the measured values is considered. As a result of these comparisons, it is desired, if necessary, to establish additional methods of protecting personnel from exposure to electromagnetic fields at work. It is also considered, the realization of a simulation of the tested conductors for a complete analyze. It is well known that modeling and simulation represent the most efficient way of optimization considering the cost-benefit ratio.

articleTitle: Analysis of Common Mode Currents and Harmonic Pollution at Supplying Induction Motors from Static Converters with Variable Modulation Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The problems of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) in three-phase systems are less studied than single-phase or direct current, due to the smaller ratio of emissions relative to the rated power of such systems. This paper is focused on the problem of emissions in three-phase variable frequency drive systems in the low-frequency EMC range, specifically on the common mode current through the connected ground wire between the static converter and power grid. The common mode current is determined to be variable depending on switching frequency. For a deeper understanding Fast Fourier Transform was used to decompose the signal. Main parameter to understand the magnitude of common mode current was the RMS of the current. The decomposition showed a significant DC component which cannot be picked up by the used RF probe, thus presenting a noise offset necessary to be considered when calculating the total effective value of common mode current. The analysis was made on the time-domain representation and the frequency behavior of the converter. The paper suggests that the standard measurement in the low-frequency range and the picked-up signal are investigated enough, as there is a disparity in the impact of emissions in the low-frequency range compared to what off-the-shelf devices have to offer, which are standard compliant, but still present considerable emissions.

articleTitle: About Analysis of Emissions from a Switched Mode Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The paper is dedicated to the analysis in the frequency domain of the currents (in common mode and differential mode) which generate conducted emissions in the supplying cable of the equipment containing a switch mode power supply (SMPS). The performed simulation considers the standard CISPR 16-1-2 which refers to specifications, methods, and test apparatus for the measurements of disturbances and immunity to conducted emissions. One proposes solutions to limit and control the conducted emissions generated by the SMPS within the supplying cable that result into noise currents and high frequency currents within the range 150 kHz – 30 MHz that might interfere with other electric equipment. Various ways to limit the mentioned emissions are simulated and analyzed. The influence of the duty-cycle over the frequency spectrum from the conducted emissions range is considered and the worst case is determined. The conclusion is that the optimum filtering solution involves the use of an EMI filter, the results being compared to the CISPR 22 standard.

articleTitle: Labscale Emulation of Abnormalities in Three-Phase Power Systems and their Preemptive Detection Using Wavelets
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: A laboratory-based system is used to emulate common anomalies in three-phase power systems. The laboratory-based system has all the modules found in the real field, but at a lower voltage level. Using the three phase lines, various common faults are simulated, and the corresponding voltages and currents are continuously logged in for all phases. The measured voltages and currents are then analyzed using wavelets. Three types of anomalies are identified using the characteristic signatures in the wavelet-based spectrograms. The combination of the already established techniques for fault location and wavelet-based anomaly detection presented in this paper, can significantly reduce the workload for the operators of energy systems dealing with maintenance and repair works, thus increasing continuity of services and reducing costs.

articleTitle: Power Quality Problems that Occur at a Company Producing Electrical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The paper presents the problems that arise when supplying a company producing electrical equipment from the electricity network. The distorting regimes that appear affect the operation of the electric power network, inducing new problems of functional nature. For their study, the authors designed and implemented a data acquisition system in order to acquire, record and transmit data on electrical quantities (three-phase voltages and currents) from the secondary winding of the transformer that supplies the company. Data were transferred to a PC running original software developed by authors, implementing analysis modules based on Fast Fourier Transform and Wavelet Packet Transform. Small differences were revealed between power quality indices computed with both methods. The performed analysis revealed significant distortions of the currents absorbed by the analyzed plant. The total current harmonic distortion and weights of the 5-th harmonic exceeded the limits stated by IEEE Std 519-2022 whilst the value of the power factor was lower than the neutral value, being associated to additional consumptions of power / reactive energy, with effect on the penalties to be paid by the company.

articleTitle: Considerations on Electromagnetic Disturbances Produced by LEDs Light Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: In this paper, a series of theoretical and practical aspects are presented in the first instance that refer to the performances of a semi-anechoic chamber that exists within the profile laboratory at the National Institute for Research, Development and Testing in Electrical Engineering – ICMET Craiova. Measurements of electromagnetic disturbances were carried out at this location, which two LED lighting devices, namely a Flexi LED & Flash light tube and a LED projector, transmitted into the power supply network. Then the authors made a comparative analysis of the practical results obtained from these measurements of electromagnetic disturbances transmitted by conduction in one of the frequency domains (from 9 kHz to 30 MHz) provided by the reference standards.

articleTitle: Using Wavelet Packet Trees to Efficiently Estimate Clustered High Order Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: This study deals with the capabilities of a 7 level Wavelet Packet tree (WPT) relative to fast estimation of joint harmonic contributions of components oscillating with frequencies higher than 2kHz. The analyzed signal from the tree’s root node spans across 7 periods such as to yield results unaffected by the edge effect. Clusters connecting nodes from the 7-th level and associated harmonics are deduced, along with flags to be used such as to obtain subtrees dedicated to each cluster for runtime savings. Tests on artificial signals with rich harmonic content and respectively with harmonics from a single cluster were made. The analysis of performance metrics revealed that 6 clusters can be used for the estimation of contributions of harmonic exceeding 2kHz, up to the limit of 4.25 kHz, while considering a threshold of at most 2.5% for the energy of individual odd harmonics to appear outside their associated cluster of nodes. An example of algorithm utilization for the output voltage of an auxiliary services converter used on a Romanian locomotive is provided.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Field Interaction Analysis With Photovoltaic Cells For Solar-Powered UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: The development of photovoltaic sources is currently contributing to new aerospace applications and the global trend is towards the increased use of green energy in both terrestrial and aerial applications. This study focuses on the possibility of using photovoltaic cells to supply electricity to consumers on board a UAV. The main objective of this study is to analyze the effects resulting from the interaction of the electrostatic field with the photovoltaic cells, mounted on the wings of a UAV, under the influence of different values of solar radiation. An experiment was conducted to validate the hypothesis proposed in this study, in which a photovoltaic structure, integrated on the surface of a NACA 0012 airfoil, was exposed to the electrostatic field produced by a Van der Graaff generator. The results show the appearance of an electrical voltage, additional to that generated by the photovoltaic system and independent of the intensity of the light radiation. These results have important practical applications, as they demonstrate the feasibility of developing photovoltaic systems capable of generating electricity independently of the existence of a light source.

articleTitle: Power Quality Impact of Electric Buses’ Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: Given the uncertainty regarding the adoption rates of electric vehicles (EV), as well as the evolution of the transport market as a result of the lack of legislation and supporting programs, as well as the types of mobility and charging infrastructure solutions, forecasting the impact of electric vehicles on the distribution grid can be challenging. It would be beneficial for grid operators to have a solid understanding of these issues once e-mobility becomes more prevalent. This paper addresses issues related to the estimated impact of large-scale implementation of electric vehicles on the power quality in Romanian power distribution system. Here are analyzed power quality parameters measured in the power distribution grid during the charging process of the electrical buses belonging to the local public transportation fleet. The results of this study are supporting the further actions designated to improve the power quality in the distribution systems, and to allow a higher integration of the EV by avoiding grid’s reliability problems and costly reinforcements.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Received Signal Strength Analysis for UAV Indoor NLOS Navigation
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: It is expected that drones will revolutionize and guide the future progress of the aerospace industry, as they are currently used to successfully complete diverse and complex missions, in both military and civilian environments. In order to carry out their missions safely, unmanned aerial vehicles require reliable and robust navigation systems. In this paper, the feasibility of an ultra-wideband (UWB) indoor positioning system will be tested and demonstrated, with the purpose of enabling drone navigation during search and rescue missions in GNSS-denied areas, such as the inside of buildings that were affected by earthquakes or other man-made calamities. The strength of the UWB (ultra-wideband) signals in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) and hard NLOS conditions was tested. The obtained results are pivotal in deciding whether UWB technology is advanced enough to guarantee the safe completion of indoor missions, without the aid of further navigation sensors.

articleTitle: Determination of Operating Characteristics for Asynchronous Generators Connected to the Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: A method for determining the operating characteristics of an asynchronous generator is proposed. An indepth study about the asynchronous machine operating as a generator connected to the power grid is performed. The use of asynchronous generators with squirrel-cage rotor is settled as a good solution due to good dynamic performances, lack of brushes, lack of an additional dc power source or low maintenance costs. Numerous simulations are developed for highlighting the advantages of the asynchronous generator connected to the grid. The proposed mathematical model allows for a settling of the operating characteristics and provides a way to perform the energy balance. These results justify the research carried out, which provides qualitatively and quantitatively correct simulations for the stationary and dynamic regime of the asynchronous generator.

articleTitle: Effects of Inrush Current on Operating Transformers when the Series Resonance Condition is Met
publicationTitle: 2023 Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility at Low Frequency (PQEMC-LF)
abstract: Inrush current often affects the quality of the power system and can interfere with the operation of sensitive electrical loads. In recent decades, studies have focused on controlling this transient current. This paper presents a case study conducted on an in-service transformer where both external and internal electric discharges occurred after several energization maneuvers. The cause of these phenomena has been identified and corrective action has been taken.
